analysis: Both units are from QwenTensorParallelBatchSessionTests.swift, a test-only file. Changes are an optional `kind` parameter on the test `Owned` init (head lines 58-61) and a new build-ahead decode test (head ~590-793). The test body past head line 469 and the patch excerpt were truncated, so the new test's body was not visible. The base unit (lines 890-1246) is pre-existing prefix-cache and SSD tier test code. It covers per-tenant partitioning, a disabled-cache partition, tier restart, balanced records and rank-unreadable-record fallback. These are unchanged by this PR in the visible ranges. The only changes are in test fixtures, which use temporary directories with synthetic keys and add no production code path, so no production behavior changes. No new attack surface, authentication, attestation or encryption change, and no data exposure or availability regression is visible. The existing tenant-isolation test assertions (T-041 cache scoping) are not weakened in the visible text. Remaining uncertainty: the new build-ahead test body is not fully visible, but as a test it carries no production security impact. The production build-ahead `submitDecode`/`readDecode` implementation is not in the supplied evidence and would need review if it is part of this PR in other batches (selection, collectives, plaintext handling).
